in_arabic.name: حامد

in_english.name: Hamed
in_english.meaning: One who praises or thanks God
in_english.long_meaning: Hamed is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning 'one who praises or thanks God'. It derives from the Arabic root H-M-D, which is also the root for 'hamd', meaning 'praise'. The name has significant religious connotations in Islam, reflecting a desirable character trait of being grateful and praising Allah. Throughout Muslim cultures, Hamed is used as a given name, reflecting the importance of humility and gratitude.

He is renowned for his works on theology and the history of Islamic science. Among his significant contributions is 'Ihya' ul-Ulum al-Qariya', a comprehensive encyclopedia covering various disciplines from Islamic sciences. This work was completed around 1188 AD.

Sheikh Hamed bin Zainal Abidin, a prominent figure in the development of Shia Islam in Malaysia, was born in 1643 AD. He was a judge, scholar, and the 12th Imam of the Shia Ithna Ashari religious tradition. Sheikh Hamed contributed significantly to the Malay language by translating various religious texts into Malay. His most famous translation is 'Al-Kafi', a collection of Hadiths, which was published in 1662 AD.
